pr_title: Add warnings for big number of completions and parallelism
pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/kind api-change

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Add a warning for Jobs when `completions > 1e5` and `parallelism > 1e4`.

In this case, the size of the field `.status.completedIndexes` might exceed the storage limits of etcd, if a big number of pod indexes fail.

- If `parallelism <= 1e4`, then the field consumes at most `(10+1)*(10^4+10^4)=0.21Mi`.
- If `completions <= 1e5`, then the field consumes at most `(5+1)*10^5=0.572Mi`

These limits are well below the default etcd limits of ~1.5Mi

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Fixes #118085

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

This warning is in accordance with the proposal in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3967.
I'll also submit a PR to update the documentation for Indexed Job.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
<!--
If no, just write "NONE" in the release-note block below.
If yes, a release note is required:
Enter your extended release note in the block below. If the PR requires additional action from users switching to the new release, include the string "action required".

For more information on release notes see: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/release-notes.md
-->
```release-note
ACTION_REQUIRED
When an Indexed Job has a number of completions higher than 10^5 and parallelism higher than 10^4, and a big number of Indexes fail, Kubernetes might not be able to track the termination of the Job. Kubernetes now emits a warning, at Job creation, when the Job manifest exceeds both of these limits.
```

issue_context.title: Indexed Jobs can break with high number of parallelism or completions
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

Currently, the maximum number of completions is MAX_INT32, around 2e9 and the maximum parallelism is 1e5.

When using these values, and assuming a very unlucky case, the field `.status.completedIndexes` can fill up the maximum size for objects in etcd (around 1.5Mi)

/sig apps
/sig scalability

### What did you expect to happen?

An Indexed Job with the maximum number of completions and parallelism to be correctly tracked.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: sample-job
spec:
  completionMode: Indexed
  completions: 2000000000
  parallelism: 100000
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: bad
        image: python
        command:
        - python3
        - -c
        - |
          import os
          import time
          id = int(os.environ.get("JOB_COMPLETION_INDEX"))
          if id > 1000000000 and id % 3 == 0:
            time.sleep(10000)
      restartPolicy: Never
```

In other words, every index multiple of 3 takes too long to terminate.

### Anything else we need to know?

In the example above, the number of characters needed by the `completedIndexes` field is:

`(10+1)*2*1e5`, roughly 2Mi, where:
- 10 is the number of characters for a number
- 1 for the separating character.
- 2 for the consecutive numbers
- 1e5 for the number of "holes" in the `completedIndexes`, based on the parallelism.

### Kubernetes version

1.21 and newer (when IndexedJob was introduced)


### Cloud provider

any

There are two possible solutions:

### Option A. Tightening validation

We can tighten validation for newly created jobs, either of maximum `parallelism`, `completions` or both. Analyzing each separately:

- `completions` would need to go down to 1e6, for a total of `(6+1)*2*1e5` bytes: ~1.33Mi. If a user needs more than this, they would need to split their job into a few, kind of like a Job slice.
- `parallelism` would need to go down 50k pods, for a total of `(10+1)*2*5e4` bytes: ~1.04Mi. If a user needs more than this for jobs with pod-to-pod communication, they are out of luck. But how realistic is the need for 100k pods where they all communicate with each other?

### Option B. Stop updating completedIndexes or creating pods when we are running out of space for completedIndexes

We can stop the Job sync when there is risk of `completedIndexes` going over the limit: do not update completedIndexes or create new pods.
This allows us to keep the same validation.
If a job is "well-behaved" (pods terminate mostly in order), users won't observe problems. But if the job behaves like the example in the description, then the job controller would stop updates, showing stale status or having a number of running pods below parallelism.

In a way, this is how the job controller would behave if we change nothing: the Job API updates will fail and will only succeed when the job controller is able to collapse `completedIndexes`.

I would lean towards option B, which roughly behaves the same as today, except that it avoids API calls that we know will fail.

But we can always do a combination of the two, without having to go as low as `1e6` for maximum number of completions.

OTOH, limiting the number of completions might be desired for the overall performance of one Job.
If users have embarrassingly parallel jobs with a high number of completions, reducing the maximum number of completions encourages them to split their workload into multiple jobs.

And they can use [JobSet](https://sigs.k8s.io/jobset) to orchestrate these jobs.

> I would lean towards option B, which roughly behaves the same as today, except that it avoids API calls that we know will fail.

that seems reasonable to me, especially given the narrow circumstances where people would actually hit this (absurdly high completions, very high parallelism, very specific completion delay/failure patterns)

> OTOH, limiting the number of completions might be desired for the overall performance of one Job.

that seems more like a policy/quota decision than an API decision

Personally, I like the idea of controlling the number of completions. When combined with JobSet it would make the Job API to play a role of a slice, allowing for scalability, yet providing a simple API for small Jobs.

OTOH I agree that the worst case scenarios are very unlikely to happen in practice, so not sure we should constrain the API capabilities due to the worst possible cases.

x-referencing the KEP discussion that initiated the discovery of the issue. There we need to make a similar decision to make sure the Job status does not grow too much: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3967#discussion_r1184118560, or the consequences are controlled.

Actually, option B wouldn't always work.

If the pods are just taking long to terminate, then yes, eventually they will complete and the `completedIndexes` field would compress and fit.

However, if the pods start failing and the job hits the backoffLimit, then those indexes won't ever be completed and we can't compress `completedIndexes` and, subsequently, mark the Job as failed.

After offline discussion with @alculquicondor and @deads2k (in the context of the backoff limit per index feature: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3967) I would like to propose the following:

* A soft limit for parallelism <= 10^4 when completions is > 10^5 (in addition to the pre-existing hard limit for parallelism). When the soft limit is violated we have a warning from the API.

When the soft limits are satisfied, then the size of the `.status.completedIndexes` field can be estimated as `(10+1)*2*10^4=210Ki`, which is way below the etcd limit of 1.5Mi. 

This approach allows:
- introduce some limits without breaking for users who are already running workloads above the soft limit
- allows users to run large jobs if they reconfigured the etcd max object size
- warn the user of the danger of running jobs above the soft limits (there will also be a user-facing documentation warning)
- is leaves the door open for supporting such scalability limits as a future work (KEP), but allows to set reasonable constraints on the backoff limit per index feature.

This approach is also compatible with the proposal for backoff limit per index KEP, there the soft limits are:
1. completions <= 10^5, parallelism <=10^5 and maxFailedIndexes <= 10^5, OR
2. completions unlimited (<= max int32), parallelism <= 10^4, maxFailedIndexes <= 10^4.

WDYT @liggitt ?
Also @jkaniuk was part of the meeting, representing SIG Scalability.
